definition.en: Formulas and shortcuts for trains crossing poles, platforms, bridges, moving persons, and opposite/same direction relative speed problems.
definition.hi: Formulas and shortcuts for trains crossing poles, platforms, bridges, moving persons, and opposite/same direction relative speed problems.

learningOutcomes.hi: समस्या समाधान में दक्षता प्राप्त करें

content.en:
Train problems apply classical relative velocity principles:
1. Crossing Stationary Point Object (pole, tree, standing man): Distance covered = Length of the train (L). Time = L / S.
2. Crossing Extended Object (platform, bridge, tunnel): Distance covered = Length of train (L) + Length of platform (P). Time = (L + P) / S.
3. Two Trains Crossing Each Other: Total distance = L₁ + L₂.
• In Opposite Directions: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
• In Same Direction: Relative Speed = |S₁ - S₂|.
4. Unit Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s and 1 m/s = 18/5 km/h.

content.en:
Illustrative Problem: A 180-meter long train running at 54 km/h crosses a 120-meter long platform. Find the time taken.
Solution:
Speed in m/s = 54 * (5/18) = 15 m/s.
Total distance = 180 + 120 = 300 m.
Time taken = 300 / 15 = 20 seconds.

question.en: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a pole in 9 seconds. How much time will it take to cross a platform 160 meters long?
question.hi: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a pole in 9 seconds. How much time will it take to cross a platform 160 meters long?

explanation.en: Speed = 72 * (5/18) = 20 m/s. Length of train = Speed * Time = 20 * 9 = 180 meters. Total distance to cross platform = 180 + 160 = 340 meters. Time taken = 340 / 20 = 17 seconds.
